title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
description: Ten no-admission ways to spend time together on campus and around Seattle, using publicly documented free access.

cards.title: Browse the Hedreen Gallery
cards.subtitle: Lee Center for the Arts, Seattle University
cards.notes: Meet at the Lee Center, take in the current exhibition together, and use the posted Wednesday–Saturday hours before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A campus gallery that is always free and open to the public.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University states that Hedreen Gallery is always free and open to the public; it is in the Lee Center for the Arts and is open Wednesday–Saturday, 1–6 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Open Wednesday–Saturday, 1–6 p.m.; the university identifies it as free and open to the public.

cards.title: Pause in the Chapel of St. Ignatius
cards.subtitle: Seattle University campus
cards.notes: Use weekday building hours for a quiet visit, or attend a listed liturgy with friends; check the chapel calendar for closures first.
cards.short_summary: Seattle U’s main chapel offers a calm shared stop during its public building hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University lists Chapel of St. Ignatius building hours as Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–4:30 p.m., and posts its Mass schedule.
cards.source_title: Chapel of St. Ignatius | Seattle University
cards.access_notes: Building hours are Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–4:30 p.m.; Sunday access is immediately before and after Mass. Check the calendar for changes.

cards.title: See art at the Frye
cards.subtitle: 704 Terry Avenue, First Hill
cards.notes: Walk over to First Hill, choose a few works to discuss, and plan around museum hours rather than a paid program or ticketed concert.
cards.short_summary: A nearby museum whose general admission is always free.
cards.evidence_claim: The Frye Art Museum states that admission is always free.
cards.access_notes: General museum admission is always free. Some separately programmed events can have registration or fees, so use the regular galleries.

cards.entity_name: Free First Thursday: Seattle Art Museum
cards.title: Do Free First Thursday at SAM
cards.subtitle: Seattle Art Museum, 1300 First Avenue
cards.notes: Put the first Thursday on the calendar, enter during the free window, and wander the galleries or join the included drop-in activities.
cards.short_summary: The downtown Seattle Art Museum has free admission on each first Thursday.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle Art Museum says admission to its downtown museum is free on the first Thursday of every month, with galleries open 10 a.m.–8 p.m.
cards.source_title: Free First Thursday | Seattle Art Museum
cards.access_notes: Free only on the first Thursday of each month; Seattle Art Museum is listed as open 10 a.m.–8 p.m. that day.

cards.entity_name: Free First Thursday: Seattle Asian Art Museum
cards.title: Visit the Asian Art Museum on First Thursday
cards.subtitle: Seattle Asian Art Museum, Volunteer Park
cards.notes: Make a first-Thursday plan around Volunteer Park, then use the free museum hours for an art-focused afternoon with your group.
cards.short_summary: The Seattle Asian Art Museum waives admission on the first Thursday each month.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle Art Museum states that Seattle Asian Art Museum admission is free on the first Thursday of every month, with hours of 10 a.m.–5 p.m.
cards.source_title: Free First Thursday | Seattle Art Museum
cards.access_notes: Free only on the first Thursday of each month; the Seattle Asian Art Museum is listed as open 10 a.m.–5 p.m.

cards.entity_name: ARTS at King Street Station Gallery
cards.title: See ARTS at King Street Station
cards.subtitle: 303 S. Jackson Street, top floor
cards.notes: Take the elevator to the top floor, view the current work at your own pace, and use Thursday evening hours when they fit the group.
cards.short_summary: A city-run gallery with regular free public hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle’s Office of Arts & Culture states that ARTS at King Street Station is free and open Wednesday–Saturday, 11 a.m.–5 p.m., with Thursday hours until 8 p.m. in 2026.
cards.source_title: ARTS at King Street Station Gallery | City of Seattle
cards.access_notes: Free Wednesday–Saturday, 11 a.m.–5 p.m.; open until 8 p.m. Thursdays in 2026. The building has an ADA-compliant elevator.

cards.entity_name: Pioneer Square First Thursday Art Walk
cards.title: Walk Pioneer Square’s First Thursday Art Walk
cards.subtitle: Pioneer Square, first Thursday of each month
cards.notes: Start at King Street Station, pick a few participating arts stops, and treat the evening as a walk-and-talk rather than a shopping outing.
cards.short_summary: A recurring neighborhood art-walk format the city describes as free.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Seattle says monthly art walks offer a free opportunity to enjoy the arts and identifies Pioneer Square’s First Thursday Art Walk as a recurring event.
cards.source_title: Art Walks | City of Seattle Office of Arts & Culture
cards.access_notes: Held on the first Thursday of the month. Individual participating businesses organize their own offerings, so confirm stops before going.

cards.title: Tour the Central Library together
cards.subtitle: Central Library, 1000 Fourth Avenue
cards.notes: Grab the self-guided tour materials, choose a route through the building’s public levels, and stop to compare favorite art or architecture details.
cards.short_summary: A self-paced architecture and art tour inside Seattle’s flagship public library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Seattle Public Library provides self-guided tour maps and an audio tour for the Central Library, and says everyone is welcome at its library locations.
cards.source_title: Take a Tour of the Central Library | The Seattle Public Library
cards.access_notes: Use the self-guided maps or audio tour during open library hours. Library system policy says everyone is welcome at its locations.

cards.title: Meet up at Capitol Hill Branch
cards.subtitle: Seattle Public Library, Capitol Hill
cards.notes: Choose a public seating area, browse together, or use the branch as a no-purchase regroup point before continuing through the neighborhood.
cards.short_summary: A public-library meet-up spot where no library card is needed simply to enter.
cards.evidence_claim: The Seattle Public Library says everyone is welcome at its library locations, including people without a library card, and lists Capitol Hill Branch among its locations.
cards.source_title: Get Started with a Library Card | The Seattle Public Library
cards.access_notes: Everyone is welcome at Seattle Public Library locations; a card is not required to enter and use many services. Check current branch hours before visiting.

cards.title: See the Soul Pole at Douglass-Truth
cards.subtitle: Douglass-Truth Branch, Seattle Public Library
cards.notes: Meet on the branch lawn to look closely at the 21-foot sculpture, then go inside to explore the branch’s public art and collection displays.
cards.short_summary: A documented community artwork at a public library branch in the Central District.
cards.evidence_claim: The Seattle Public Library identifies the Soul Pole on the Douglass-Truth Branch lawn as a 21-foot wooden sculpture depicting African American history, and says everyone is welcome at its library locations.
cards.source_title: Douglass-Truth Branch Art | The Seattle Public Library
cards.access_notes: The Soul Pole is on the branch lawn. Enter the library during posted branch hours; Seattle Public Library says everyone is welcome at its locations.
